summary: pyNeuroML 1.3.22 (PyPI, 2026-06-02, LGPL-3.0-only) is the actively maintained Python front end. Its wheel ships the jNeuroML 0.14.0 jar-with-dependencies (pyneuroml/lib/jNeuroML-0.14.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar, 28,904,516 bytes) but does not ship a Java runtime: every jnml-backed call (validation, jLEMS simulation, NEURON/NetPyNE/Brian export) shells out to 'java -jar' and needs java on PATH. jNeuroML's latest GitHub release is v0.14.0 (2025-02-12, LGPL-3.0, compiled for Java 1.8, CI-tested on Java 8-21 incl. windows-2019). Schema validation without Java is available through libNeuroML 0.6.7 (neuroml.utils.is_valid_neuroml2 / validate_neuroml2, generateDS constraints derived from NeuroML_v2.3.1.xsd) and via lxml against the XSD files shipped inside libNeuroML; both were confirmed empirically on Windows 11 / Python 3.12.10 in a scratch venv. Relevant APIs exist and were verified in source at tag v1.3.22: pyneuroml.validators.validate_neuroml2, pyneuroml.runners.run_lems_with_jneuroml / run_jneuroml / run_lems_with_jneuroml_neuron / reload_saved_data, pyneuroml.utils.simdata.load_sim_data_from_lems_file, pyneuroml.lems.LEMSSimulation, pyneuroml.lems.generate_lems_file_for_neuroml, pyneuroml.analysis.generate_current_vs_frequency_curve and analyse_spiketime_vs_dt. Pitfalls found: without Java the jnml-backed validator and runner return bare False (indistinguishable from an invalid model); run_lems_with_jneuroml(skip_run=True) raises UnboundLocalError in 1.3.22 (also unchanged on master when fetched); validate_neuroml2_lems_file hard-codes exit_on_fail=True (sys.exit on failure). No Java is installed on this machine, so no jLEMS simulation or NEURON export was executed in this audit.
latest_version: pyNeuroML 1.3.22 (bundles jNeuroML 0.14.0); standalone jNeuroML latest GitHub release v0.14.0
license_spdx: LGPL-3.0-only (pyNeuroML, per PyPI metadata and setup.cfg); jNeuroML: GitHub detects LGPL-3.0 from LICENSE.lesser (only vs or-later not verified)
python_requires: Not declared (PyPI info.requires_python is null; setup.cfg at v1.3.22 has no python_requires). Classifiers list Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14; CI matrix tests 3.10-3.14 on ubuntu-latest. Install verified on Python 3.12.10 (Windows 11) in a scratch venv.
other_runtime_requirements: Java runtime (JRE) on PATH is mandatory for all jNeuroML-backed functions (not bundled; README lists JRE as dependency). jNeuroML 0.14.0 compiled with source/target 1.8; its CI tests Temurin Java 8, 11, 16, 17, 19, 21. Default JVM max heap 400M, overridable via env JNML_MAX_MEMORY_LOCAL or max_memory argument / pynml -java_max_memory. Core Python deps: pylems>=0.6.8, airspeed>=0.5.5, neuromllite>=0.6.1, libNeuroML>=0.6.7, matplotlib, matplotlib-scalebar, progressbar2, graphviz, lxml, numpy, sympy, ppft[dill] (resolved in venv: PyLEMS 0.6.9, libNeuroML 0.6.7, neuromllite 0.6.1, lxml 6.1.3, numpy 2.5.3, tables 3.11.1, matplotlib 3.11.2). README also lists Graphviz 'dot'. Optional: NEURON (+pyyaml) via extra [neuron] for -neuron runs; pyelectro via extra [analysis] needed by generate_current_vs_frequency_curve; Brian2, netpyne, etc. via other extras.
maintenance_status: pyNeuroML: actively maintained - 1.3.22 released 2026-06-02, earlier 1.3.21 on 2025-07-22; master commits through 2026-07-21 (numpy unpin, dropping EOL Python, CI dependency bumps). jNeuroML: stable, low activity - last release v0.14.0 on 2025-02-12; last commit on 'development' branch 2025-02-12; default branch 'master' last commit 2024-08-20 and its pom.xml still says 0.13.3 (release built from development/tag). Repository not archived.
windows_support: Partially verified. pyNeuroML is pure-Python plus a jar and installs on Windows 11 / Python 3.12.10 (verified). Pure-Python validation (libNeuroML, lxml+XSD) works on Windows (verified). pyNeuroML CI runs only on ubuntu-latest, so Windows is not CI-tested for pyNeuroML. jNeuroML's own CI (v0.14.0) includes windows-2019 across Java 8-21, and the jNeuroML distribution provides jnml.bat for Windows. Source-level Windows specifics in pyneuroml.runners: -Djava.awt.headless=true is skipped when os.name == 'nt'; commands run with subprocess shell=True; _include_string builds " -I '<paths joined by :>'" - the ':' separator collides with Windows drive letters and cmd.exe does not strip single quotes (potential include-path bug; NOT tested because Java is absent). No Java on this machine: jnml validation and jLEMS runs failed with 'java' not recognized and returned False. Recommendation: run the frozen study in a Linux container or WSL with a pinned JRE; keep Windows for pure-Python checks.

facts.claim: jLEMS numerical integration scheme as described in the LEMS paper
facts.value: Cannon RC, Gleeson P, Crook S, Ganapathy G, Marin B, Piasini E, Silver RA. LEMS: a language for expressing complex biological models in concise and hierarchical form and its use in underpinning NeuroML 2. Front Neuroinform 8 (2014), doi 10.3389/fninf.2014.00079, PMC4174883. Paper describes jLEMS default evaluation with a simple forward Euler scheme, a flattened mode using 4th-order Runge-Kutta, and PyLEMS using forward Euler. Whether jNeuroML 0.14.0 still defaults to forward Euler was not verified in current source

reuse_for_neurosem: Pin pyNeuroML==1.3.22 (brings libNeuroML 0.6.7, PyLEMS 0.6.9, neuromllite 0.6.1) and use its bundled jNeuroML 0.14.0 jar; no separate jNeuroML download is needed, but a pinned JRE (e.g. Temurin in the Docker image) is required. Record jar SHA-256, JNEUROML_VERSION, java -version output and pip freeze in every run manifest.

Structural validity: use jnml -validate through pyneuroml.validators.validate_neuroml2(..., return_string=True) as the authoritative check (schema plus jnml's additional tests), preceded by a Java-free pre-check with neuroml.utils.is_valid_neuroml2 and/or lxml XSD validation against libNeuroML's shipped NeuroML_v2.3.1.xsd.

Execution: use pyneuroml.runners.run_jneuroml / run_lems_with_jneuroml (nogui=True, exit_on_fail=False, load_saved_data=True, per-run exec_in_dir) for jLEMS simulations; run_multiple_lems_with for parallelism.
Trace loading: reload_saved_data or pyneuroml.utils.simdata.load_sim_data_from_lems_file / load_traces_from_data_file to turn saved OutputFile .dat columns into numpy arrays for eFEL.

LEMS generation: pyneuroml.lems.LEMSSimulation (duration, dt, target, output columns, simulation_seed) to build per-protocol and per-dt (h, h/2, h/4) simulation files; libNeuroML object model (e.g. PulseGenerator, Population, InputList) to attach stimuli.
Model I/O for mutation and valid-transformation operators: pyneuroml.io.read_neuroml2_file / write_neuroml2_file (or libNeuroML loaders/writers).
Optional cross-simulator checks: run_lems_with_jneuroml_neuron / pynml -neuron -run for NEURON export (needs NEURON installed).
Sanity baselines: generate_current_vs_frequency_curve for a coarse f-I/rheobase bracket and analyse_spiketime_vs_dt as a reference dt-sensitivity check; do not claim novelty for these.
not_provided_new_for_neurosem: A robust tool-health and error taxonomy: pyNeuroML's jnml wrappers return bare False both for an invalid/non-executable model and for a missing Java runtime, and some paths call sys.exit; NeuroSem must detect Java presence/version, capture output, and classify structurally invalid vs non-executable vs tool failure vs numerically unstable.

Protocol engine beyond fixed-amplitude pulse grids: rheobase bisection search (pyNeuroML's f-I threshold is only the lowest tested amplitude that spiked), rheobase-normalised amplitudes, long step, ramp, hyperpolarising step, hyperpolarisation-release rebound, short pulse, paired pulses, chirp, with independent timing/amplitude tests. (Which of these NeuroML core input component types can express directly is for the NeuroML/LEMS audit to verify.)
eFEL integration (pyNeuroML analysis uses pyelectro), including frozen eFEL settings, stimulation-window handling and explicit undefined-feature handling (never zero-filling).

Numerical-refinement tolerance calibration: running h, h/2, h/4, aligning traces on a common grid, per-feature absolute/relative floors and frozen tau rules; analyse_spiketime_vs_dt only compares spike times across dts.
Controlled single-fault mutation operators (stimulus, biophysical, reference, numerical families), one-change enforcement, mutant provenance and the admissibility classification.
Valid-transformation generators (unit conversion, formatting, renames, factoring, reordering, explicit defaults) and their verification.
Perturbation fingerprints, the mutant-by-protocol detection matrix, greedy max-coverage selection, count- and runtime-matched random baselines, exhaustive-battery comparison.
Held-out model and mutation-family split management, leakage barriers, split hashing and held-out access logging.
Run-level provenance manifests (hashes, environment digest, jar hash, Java version, runtime, trace/feature hashes, Git commit); pyNeuroML only logs the executed command.
Per-protocol runtime/cost measurement for runtime-matched baselines and detection-versus-cost curves.
Statistical analysis (clustered resampling by base model, exact paired tests, tolerance sensitivity).
handoff_assumption_issues: Correct but incomplete: the handoff lists pyNeuroML/jNeuroML for parsing, validation, simulation and translation. Verified, but all jNeuroML functionality requires a Java runtime that pyNeuroML does not bundle; the audit machine has no Java, and system-wide installs are outside M0 rules. M1's 'one command validates and simulates both models' therefore needs a decision on how Java is provided (Docker/Linux image with pinned JRE, WSL, or a user-level JRE).

Uncertain for Windows: pyNeuroML CI runs only on ubuntu-latest; source shows Windows-sensitive include-path construction (colon-joined, single-quoted -I argument under shell=True). The handoff's Dockerfile/CI plan should treat Linux as the reference platform for the frozen study.

Validation cascade risk: pyneuroml validate_neuroml2 and run_lems_with_jneuroml return False when Java is missing, indistinguishable from an invalid or non-executable mutant; validate_neuroml2_lems_file and default run_lems_with_jneuroml (exit_on_fail=True) can terminate the process. The handoff's mutant classification (structurally invalid / non-executable / ...) needs NeuroSem-side tool-health checks and exit_on_fail=False.

API caveat: run_lems_with_jneuroml(skip_run=True), the natural 'parse only' option, raises UnboundLocalError in 1.3.22 (unchanged on master when fetched). Use jnml -validate / -norun via run_jneuroml instead.

'jNeuroML only' pilot is consistent with starting from single-compartment models: NeuroML docs describe jLEMS as suited to single-compartment models, with multicompartmental cells needing NEURON or similar. The full study's multicompartment models imply a second simulator (NEURON via -neuron), which changes numerical behaviour and must be handled in tolerances.

Tolerance calibration by h, h/2, h/4: the 2014 LEMS paper describes jLEMS default integration as forward Euler (first order), so refinement differences may be large and slowly converging; whether jNeuroML 0.14.0 still uses that default is unverified. Budget smaller dt and longer runtimes, and verify the integrator before M5.

Mutation family 'Numerical: solver configuration': LEMSSimulation exposes duration, dt and seeds but no integration-method argument; for a jNeuroML-only pilot, solver-configuration mutants may not be expressible and should be restricted to dt/output-sampling until verified.

Schema version must be frozen explicitly: jNeuroML 0.14.0 release notes reference NeuroML v2.3.1 and libNeuroML 0.6.7 is generated from NeuroML_v2.3.1.xsd; 'current NeuroML validity' in model selection should name v2.3.1 (or whatever is verified in the NeuroML audit).

Dependency pinning: pyNeuroML declares no requires_python, so pip will not stop installs on unsupported Pythons; pin Python (3.12 verified locally; classifiers 3.10-3.14) and lock transitive versions (numpy 2.5.3, tables 3.11.1 etc. resolved on 2026-09-13).

Licensing to record in LICENSE_AUDIT: pyNeuroML LGPL-3.0-only; jNeuroML LGPL-3.0 (GitHub detection); jLEMS MIT; org.neuroml.export/model and NeuroML2 LGPL-3.0; libNeuroML metadata says BSD-2-Clause while its LICENSE text/GitHub detection indicate BSD-3-Clause. Compatibility of NeuroSem's chosen license with LGPL dependencies (used as unmodified libraries/jar) should be confirmed by Neel; this audit is not legal advice.

Built-in f-I utility is coarse: generate_current_vs_frequency_curve does not implement rheobase search (per its docstring) and needs pyelectro; the handoff's rheobase-normalised protocols require new NeuroSem code.
uncertainties: No jLEMS simulation, jnml -validate run, or NEURON export was executed (no Java, no NEURON on the audit machine); runtime behaviour, output formats and determinism are verified from source/docs only.

Whether jLEMS inside jNeuroML 0.14.0 still defaults to forward Euler (source for this is the 2014 LEMS paper, not current code).
Whether the -I include-path string (colon separator, single quotes) breaks on Windows cmd.exe; not tested.
